{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-10-12: "I feel like we run everything locally and then run CI checks on top of it. The end result is that it takes like ~1 hour or more to get a simple change small change like rewording of a skill to be merged."

WHAT THE HOUR WAS MADE OF ON 2026-10-12, as observed in the session (not timed step by step): a new worktree per change, whose first cargo build compiles RocksDB from cold (the project's own rule puts that at about 34 minutes, rule:never-a-bare-cargo-clean-on-the-dev-box); local tests; the design hold, record and copy for the PR; then CI's long job of 16–25 minutes; then waiting for the owner's named merge.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) CI is the gate. Locally, run only what the change touches (for a skill rewording: the skill lint and its suite, the init suite, the findability test), push, and let CI run everything once. Cost: a CI failure costs another push and another CI run.
(b) The local run is the gate and CI is advisory for small changes. Cost: a local run is not independent and leaves no shared record; this project's CI exists partly because local runs were subsets read as the whole.
(c) Keep both, but stop paying the cold build locally: reuse one worktree per line of work, or a compiler cache shared across worktrees (safe, unlike a shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR, which built another branch's code).
(d) Remove the per-PR design ritual instead: req:a-nightly-check-on-the-box-runs-reflow2s-client-against-the-hosted-design-and-the-copy-retires is ACCEPTED intent, not yet built, and retires the hold, the per-PR copy and its gate. That is a different lever on the same hour, and it is already decided, not an idea.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT to (a) and (b), on the record: running a subset of the gate set and reading it as the whole happened four times in one day (fact:a-local-feature-error-was-worked-around-instead-of-read-as-the-ci-contract). (a) is safe only because CI still runs everything before a merge; (b) gives that up.

WHICH IS CHEAPER: (a) and (c) need no code, only a change in how the work is done; (d) is real work already decided; (b) is cheap in minutes and expensive in assurance.
